result: A library of ~1000 Drosophila stocks with T2A-GAL4 insertions was generated, comprising 619 MiMIC conversions and 388 CRIMIC insertions.
evaluation: Claims C1, C24, and C25 collectively document the creation of the library with specific numbers (619 + 388 ≈ 1000). The methodology is described in detail throughout the manuscript with supporting data and figures.

result: Approximately 90% of T2A-GAL4 insertions in essential genes cause severe loss-of-function phenotypes as demonstrated by complementation testing.
evaluation: Claims C2, C61, C62, and C77 provide converging evidence: 100 genes were tested using deficiencies, 90 failed to complement, 5 were semi-lethal, and 5 were viable. The 90% figure is directly supported by experimental data (Figure 4B, Supplementary file 2).

result: Most CRISPR-engineered chromosomes do not carry second-site lethal mutations, as demonstrated by FLP-mediated excision and genomic rescue experiments.
evaluation: Claims C3, C63-C65, and C86 provide multiple lines of evidence: 8/11 X-chromosome insertions were rescued by UAS-FLP, the three failures showed efficient cassette excision, and all were rescued by P[acman] clones. However, the abstract claims 12/14 while the text shows 8/11 tested, creating a minor inconsistency in the exact numbers.

result: Approximately 70% (26/36) of lethal insertions can be rescued with a single UAS-cDNA construct, regardless of tag presence or number of protein isoforms.
evaluation: Claims C4, C89-C91 are supported by Table 1 data showing 25/36 rescued (69.4%). Statistical analysis (Chi sq. = 0.0004, p=0.98) confirms no pattern related to tag presence. The result is notable given that most genes encode multiple isoforms.

result: Loss-of-function phenotypes can be reverted by FLP-mediated excision of the T2A-GAL4 cassette in most cases, enabling conditional rescue experiments.
evaluation: Claims C5, C63, C66, C87, and C88 demonstrate that 8/11 lethal insertions were rescued by UAS-FLP (Figure 4C). The data support the utility of this approach for assessing gene requirements, though the mechanism failed for 3 genes despite efficient excision.

result: T2A-GAL4 driven UAS-GFP/RFP provides high sensitivity detection of gene expression, particularly in adult brains where only ~19% of GFSTF-tagged genes showed robust signals.
evaluation: Claims C6, C35-C37, and C78-C80 demonstrate the enhanced sensitivity of T2A-GAL4 over GFSTF tagging. Figure 1 shows robust signals in adult brains with T2A-GAL4 where GFSTF showed weak/no signal. The 19% detection rate for GFSTF (114/611) versus robust T2A-GAL4 signals supports the sensitivity claim.

result: Expression patterns of hundreds of previously unreported genes were documented, including 7 novel tracheal genes, 12 novel glial genes, and 18 novel PI neuron genes.
evaluation: Claims C7, C93, C94, C96, C99, and C106 document novel expression patterns for specific gene categories. The study examined 550 genes in adult brains (C93), with ~80% showing expression (C94). Specific novel patterns are documented with figures (Figure 5, supplements 1-3) and compared to FlyBase annotations.

result: The inserted cassettes can be replaced with other DNA sequences through RMCE, as demonstrated by the modular vector design with attP sites.
evaluation: Claims C8, C17, and C45-C47, C53 describe the technical capability for cassette exchange. The MiMIC and CRIMIC vectors contain attP sites flanking the cassettes, enabling RMCE with attB-containing constructs. This is a design feature supported by prior work (C17 citations) and demonstrated through the conversion experiments.

result: CRIMIC technology achieves ~70% integration efficiency (80% excluding third chromosome) with optimized injection parameters of 25 ng/µl sgRNA and 150 ng/µl donor DNA.
evaluation: Claims C50-C52, C55-C58, C73-C74 document the optimization process and success rates. Initial vectors pM14 (57%) and pM36 (26%) were abandoned. The optimized pM37 achieved 70% success (388/557 genes), or ~80% excluding problematic third chromosome targets (C60, C74). Data are presented in Figure 4A.

result: MiMIC T2A-GAL4 conversion achieved 68.1% success on first attempt and 41.1% on second attempt, with the technology capable of tagging at least half of Drosophila genes.
evaluation: Claims C67-C70 provide specific success rates: 543/797 (68.1%) first attempt, 76/185 (41.1%) second attempt, with 109/797 failing twice. The projection that half the genome is taggable (C70) is reasonable given that ~5822 genes have suitable introns and technical success rates are 68-80%.

result: T2A-GAL4 driven mCD8::GFP amplifies expression but loses subcellular protein distribution information compared to GFSTF tagging.
evaluation: Claims C40-C42 describe the tradeoff between sensitivity and resolution. Figure 1—figure supplement 2 shows overlap for arm, Mhc, and osa at low resolution, but discrepancies for trio. This is an expected consequence of the GAL4/UAS amplification system versus direct protein tagging.

result: T2A-GAL4 expression patterns are validated by comparison with published antibody staining and known expression patterns.
evaluation: Claims C39 and C107 provide validation through comparison with published data. GFSTF patterns match antibody staining for Cactus, Rgk1, Dlg1, and Bruchpilot (C39). T2A-GAL4 patterns for AstA-R2 and Lkr in PI neurons agree with prior observations (C107). This supports the fidelity of the approach.

result: The MiMIC collection comprises ~15,660 insertions, with 2854 intronic insertions in 1862 genes classified as Gold (1399), Silver (550), or Bronze (193) based on transcript coverage.
evaluation: Claims C26-C33 describe the prior MiMIC resource that forms the foundation for this work. The numbers are consistent and cited to prior publications (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015b). The classification system (Gold/Silver/Bronze) is clearly defined based on transcript coverage.

result: GFSTF tagging shows robust signals in 90% of third instar larval brains but only ~19% of adult brains.
evaluation: Claims C34 and C35 document a developmental difference in detection sensitivity. The 90% figure for larvae is from prior work (C34, cited), while the 19% for adult brains (114/611) is from this study (C35, Figure 1—figure supplement 1). This motivated the development of the more sensitive T2A-GAL4 approach.

result: The CRIMIC production pipeline has ~80% cloning success and requires ~50 hours of work per characterized stock, with ~45-50% of fly genes theoretically taggable.
evaluation: Claims C71, C72, and C75 provide practical information about the technology. The 80% cloning success (C71) and 50-hour labor estimate (C75) are stated but not extensively documented. The 45-50% genome coverage estimate (C72) is reasonable given that genes without suitable introns cannot be targeted.

result: Expression pattern analysis of 550 genes revealed tissue-specific categories: 2% trachea, ~3.5% glia, and ~80% neurons in adult brains.
evaluation: Claims C95, C97, and C102 provide categorical breakdown of expression patterns. The percentages are directly stated: 9/550 (2%) trachea, 19/550 (~3.5%) glia, and ~80% neurons. These are supported by Figure 5 and supplements showing representative examples.

result: The CRIMIC methodology uses Golden Gate Assembly for donor construction, isogenized nos-Cas9 flies for injection, and PCR validation of all insertions.
evaluation: Claims C48-C49, C54, C59-C60 describe methodological details. Golden Gate Assembly with ~1 kb homology arms (C48), isogenized injection strains (C49), optimized injection concentrations (C54), and PCR validation (C59) are all documented. The technical limitation with third chromosome efficiency (C60) is acknowledged.

result: The cassette design uses a splice acceptor from Mhc intron 18, a T2A ribosomal skipping site, and a polyA signal to generate GAL4 while truncating endogenous transcripts.
evaluation: Claims C76, C21, and C22 describe the molecular design. The SA from Mhc intron 18 has been used previously (C76, multiple citations). The T2A mechanism (C22) and polyA function (C21) are well-established and cited. The 90% loss-of-function rate (C77) validates the effectiveness of this design.

result: The T2A-GAL4 approach differs from Janelia/VDRC GAL4 collections by preserving endogenous regulatory context rather than using isolated enhancer fragments.
evaluation: Claims C81-C84 compare this approach to existing resources. The Janelia/VDRC collections use isolated 2-3 kb enhancer fragments for sparse labeling (C82-C83), while T2A-GAL4 preserves endogenous context. This is a conceptual distinction supported by citations (Jenett et al., 2012; Pfeiffer et al., 2008) and enables future comparative studies (C84).

result: The study builds on extensive prior Drosophila genetic tools including P-element enhancer traps, GAL4/UAS systems, MiMIC technology, and Trojan GAL4.
evaluation: Claims C9-C20, C23 provide historical context and cite prior work extensively. These are background claims describing established technologies (enhancer traps, GAL4/UAS, Split-GAL4, MARCM, MiMIC, GFSTF tagging, Trojan GAL4) that form the foundation for the current work. All claims are properly cited.

result: Prior work showed that MiMIC manipulations can induce second-site mutations and GFSTF tagging disrupts ~25% of genes.
evaluation: Claims C85 and C92 cite prior findings about limitations of earlier approaches. These are properly attributed to previous publications (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015b; Venken et al., 2011a) and provide context for why validation experiments (FLP excision, genomic rescue) were performed in this study.

result: Background biological knowledge about specific genes and cell types (trio, ry, PI neurons, glia) is cited to provide context for expression pattern findings.
evaluation: Claims C43-C44, C100-C101, C103-C105, C108-C109 provide biological context from the literature. These are properly cited background claims about gene functions (trio, rosy), neuroanatomy (PI neurons), and cell type composition (glia percentages in fly vs. mammalian brains) that help interpret the expression pattern data.

result: Seven genes with known glial expression and two genes with known PI neuron expression serve as positive controls validating the T2A-GAL4 approach.
evaluation: Claims C98 and C107 identify genes with previously documented expression patterns that match T2A-GAL4 results. These serve as internal validation: CIC-a, loco, CG10702, CG6126, Gs2, Egfr, Tret1-1 for glia (C98) and AstA-R2, Lkr for PI neurons (C107). Agreement with prior work supports the fidelity of the method.
